item.title: Implement atomic ledger per SPEC.md with focused tests
item.brief: Implement ledger.py according to SPEC.md. Preserve exactly the documented API and handle every specified error and boundary case. Add focused standard-library unittest coverage beyond the two existing basic tests, including constructor validation (including bool rejection, bounds, names, non-dict), copying/snapshot isolation, amount validation before account lookup, unknown accounts, insufficient funds, destination overflow, self-transfer semantics at MAX_BALANCE, unchanged state on failures, and thread linearizability/snapshot atomicity with deterministic coordination (no random inputs or wall-clock calculations). Use only Python standard library. Run the relevant tests and commit the work on this item's local branch. Do not push. Follow repository guidance if present, and keep the change limited to the module and focused tests. Acceptance: all SPEC.md behaviors are implemented and covered; existing tests pass; a commit is created.

pr.body: Added built-in dict/name/balance and amount validation, preserving amount validation before account lookup. Constructor inputs and returned snapshots are copied. A per-ledger lock protects account lookup, funds and overflow checks, writes, self-transfers, and snapshots. Added tests for boundaries, bool rejection, isolation, errors, unchanged failure state, self-transfer at MAX_BALANCE, opposite transfers, and snapshot behavior. Verification: python -B -m unittest -v (10 passed); git diff --check (passed). Assumption: account names are validated with isinstance(str), matching the documented string requirement.
pr.summary: Implemented the bounded, thread-safe ledger and focused edge-case coverage. Before: ledger methods were unimplemented; now: transfers and snapshots are atomic with validated inputs.
pr.title: Implement atomic thread-safe ledger

risk.why: The implementation changes concurrent state mutation and locking behavior. One lock protects all checks, writes, and snapshots; independent review found no blocking defects. Reviewer noted the snapshot test does not guarantee the snapshot thread attempts its read during the paused transfer.
